hints: Recall the definition of power as the rate at which work is done: $P = \frac{W}{t}$.
Substitute the work done $W = 750000\text{ J}$ and the time interval $t = 10\text{ s}$ into the formula.
Calculate the numerical value and state your final answer in watts ($\text{W}$) or kilowatts ($\text{kW}$).
walkthrough:
Use the definition of power as the rate of doing work:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$

Substitute $W = 750000\text{ J}$ and $t = 10\text{ s}$ to calculate the engine power:
$$P = \frac{750000}{10} = 75000\text{ W} = 75\text{ kW}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Applies $P = W/t = 750000/10$ to obtain $75000\text{ W}$ or $75\text{ kW}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the foundational formula relating power, work done, and time:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$
Here $P$ is the power of the engine in watts, $W$ is the work done in joules, and $t$ is the elapsed time in seconds.

Substitute the given values $W = 750000\text{ J}$ and $t = 10\text{ s}$ directly into the equation:
$$P = \frac{750000}{10}$$

Perform the division to find the power:
$$P = 75000\text{ W}$$
Dividing by $1000$ expresses this equivalently in kilowatts as $75\text{ kW}$.

hints: Connect the engine power $P = 75000\text{ W}$ to the forward driving force $F_D$ at speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $P = F_D v$.
Set up Newton's second law in the forward horizontal direction: $F_D - R = ma$, where $R = 2400\text{ N}$ and $m = 16000\text{ kg}$.
Substitute $F_D = 3000\text{ N}$ into the equation of motion and solve for the acceleration $a$.
walkthrough:
Use $P = F_D v$ to find the driving force of the engine at $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{75000}{25} = 3000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the direction of motion with resistance $R = 2400\text{ N}$ and mass $m = 16000\text{ kg}$:
$$F_D - R = ma$$
$$3000 - 2400 = 16000a$$

Solve for the acceleration $a$:
$$600 = 16000a$$
$$a = \frac{600}{16000} = 0.0375\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Finds driving force $F = 75000/25 = 3000\text{ N}$ and forms $3000 - 2400 = 16000a$ to obtain $a = 0.0375\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Rearrange to make the driving force $F_D$ the subject:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute the power from part (a) $P = 75000\text{ W}$ and the instantaneous speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{75000}{25} = 3000\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for horizontal motion in the forward direction:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$
Substitute the driving force $F_D = 3000\text{ N}$, resistance force $R = 2400\text{ N}$, and mass $m = 16000\text{ kg}$:
$$3000 - 2400 = 16000a$$

Simplify the left side and solve for the acceleration $a$:
$$600 = 16000a$$
Divide both sides by $16000$:
$$a = \frac{600}{16000} = \frac{3}{80} = 0.0375\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
